Seeing a satellite’s pose through one eye

TGP-UTF estimates the 6-DoF pose of a non-cooperative satellite from a single monocular frame, and carries a per-keypoint uncertainty through every stage that follows.

What this project does

A chaser spacecraft meeting a dead satellite or a piece of debris gets no help from the target: no markers, no radio, no GPS. TGP-UTF finds eight landmarks on the target in a single camera image, solves for pose with a geometric solver, and tracks it over time. The key idea: the uncertainty (σ) each keypoint predicts is reused to weight the solver, to pick trustworthy pseudo-labels, and to set the Kalman filter’s measurement noise.

It targets autonomous rendezvous and docking, the situation ISRO’s SpaDeX mission faces. The data comes from a real hardware-in-the-loop rig at ISITE, URSC, not synthetic renders.

Five stages, one uncertainty signal

Select a stage to see what it does and how far it has got.

A real rig, not renders

An OAK-D camera and Jetson Nano on a robotic arm swept a satellite mock-up through a wide range of poses at the ISITE URSC HILS lab, giving 983 image and pose pairs. Only the camera pose was recorded, so every keypoint label was generated: an 8-point CAD model (four body corners, two panel/antenna tips, thruster, docking-port origin) was reprojected using calibrated intrinsics and a 14-coefficient distortion model, then ground-truth pose was re-fitted by PnP so training and evaluation share one convention. Eight frames with unreliable silhouette ratios were removed.

Results

All numbers are from the 98 validation frames. Pick a Stage 2 variant to compare. Rotation, translation and ADD for the CLAHE and attention variants were measured before the rot180Z correction, so keypoint pixel error is the fair comparison.

The 180° puzzle

Keypoints were accurate to a few pixels, yet rotation error sat at 179–180°. A sweep of every candidate axis correction isolated one transform, Rz(180°). The label pipeline checks out against itself with 0.00° residual, so this is a real two-fold PnP ambiguity: the target’s keypoints are nearly symmetric about its own Z-axis.

Mean rotation error

Open issueTranslation error stays near 16 m, which points to a separate scale or reference-frame problem. Fixing it is the next job.

The σ gate

Keypoints whose predicted σ exceeds a threshold are dropped before PnP. Drag the threshold to see the idea on eight example keypoints. The σ values here are illustrative, not measured.

Run it

The repository holds the Colab notebook for the full Stage 1–5 pipeline and demo. The dataset is not included; you need authorised access.

git clone https://github.com/yehaa2004/Satellite-Pose-Estimation-TGP-UTF-.git
pip install torch torchvision timm
pip install numpy scipy opencv-python-headless
pip install filterpy matplotlib scikit-learn tqdm
# open the notebook in Colab, set ZIP_PATH to your dataset, run cells in order

Stack: PyTorch, timm (ViT-Small), OpenCV (RANSAC-EPnP, LM), filterpy (UKF), NumPy/SciPy.

Limitations, stated plainly

The σ threshold was tuned on the validation split; there is one lab mock-up and no on-orbit imagery; Stages 4 and 5 have outputs but no quantified adaptation or jitter metrics; graph (GCN) refinement is a proposed extension, not implemented; onboard latency is unbenchmarked.
